First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x
$$

Substituting $x={67.5}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2{sin}^{2}⁡({67.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {67.5}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
